title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.83-85). Grothendieck is testing his axioms for 'magmas/mosaics' (axioms Mag 1-4, then 'Mog L1, L2', the axioms of divisibility and separation) on a model built from a poset L. The objects are 'points' P_x (x in L), with support |P_x| = {x}, and 'segments' S_{a,b} (a<b), with support [a,b] and interior ]a,b[. Strangeness (disjointness) is defined combinatorially: P_x |o| P_y iff x and y are distinct and comparable, written x || y. P_x |o| S_{a,b} iff x<=a or x>=b. S_{a,b} |o| S_{a',b'} iff b<=a' or b'<=a. On p.83 he checks Mag 1-4.

This page.
(1) The divisibility axiom Mog L1 says every S_{a,b} has nonempty interior. Here that means L is dense ('divisible'): a<b implies there is x with a<x<b.
(2) He asks whether L1 implies Mog L2 and starts writing 'No, example' (crossed out). He unpacks L2 in two cases:
- (a) for P_x and S_{a,b}: if x is comparable with and distinct from every element of ]a,b[, then x<=a or x>=b.
- (b) for two segments: if ]a,b[ || ]a',b'[ elementwise, then b<=a' or b'<=a. He notes (b) is a consequence of (a).
(3) Lemma: Mog L2 holds iff (i) L is divisible and (ii) for all x and all a<b, x || ]a,b[ implies x<=a or x>=b.
(4) Equivalent form (iii), order-continuity:
- (a) for every non-maximal a, the intersection over c>a of L_{<=c} equals L_{<=a};
- (b) dually, for every non-minimal b, the intersection over c<b of L_{>=c} equals L_{>=b}.
(5) He remarks that this is usually not satisfied by posets arising from topological situations. The sketch shows a lens-shaped region from 0 to 1 with vertical strips a and b and a strip x near b, ordered left to right; x is comparable with everything strictly between a and b without lying outside [a,b] in the required sense.

Where it leads. On p.85 he shows the model is 'faithful' (disjoint interiors imply strangeness) iff L is totally ordered. It is 'perfect' iff L is a dense total order, i.e. a combinatorial model of the 1-dimensional continuum (the real interval). This page is the intermediate step isolating density plus an order-continuity condition.
errors: (ii)+(i) implies (iii) checks out. If y<=c for all c>a and a<b, density excludes y>a. For z in ]a,b[ we get y<z, so y || ]a,b[, and (ii) gives y<=a.
The converse (iii) implies (ii) is not obvious. (iii)a intersects over all c>a, while (ii) only gives information about c in ]a,b[. An argument or extra hypothesis seems needed.
It is also unclear whether (iii) alone forces divisibility. It does in the totally ordered case, where a cover relation a<b immediately violates (iii)a. In general posets a proof is missing.

Note (iii) is not equivalent to (ii) alone: the two-element chain a<b satisfies (ii) vacuously but fails (iii). So the later insertion of '(i) L div.' was necessary, and Grothendieck evidently corrected this himself.
The claim that (b) follows from (a) is stated without proof; it is plausible (apply (a) to the points of ]a,b[).
The initial 'No, example' (L1 does not imply L2) is crossed out without an example.

ideas.what: Combinatorial point/segment model M(L) attached to a poset L, used to test the axioms of an abstract 'analysis situs' (magmas/mosaics with strangeness relation |o| and refinement relation)
ideas.modern_name: incidence/betweenness structures; order-theoretic models of the line; combinatorial tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (in spirit: Hilbert's order axioms, Huntington/Veblen betweenness, synthetic topology)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished 'Analysis situs' notes (1986); Esquisse d'un programme mentions tame topology only in general terms

ideas.what: Divisibility axiom equivalent to density of L
Separation axiom Mog L2 equivalent to density plus order-continuity: the intersection over c>a of down-sets L_{<=c} equals L_{<=a}, and dually
ideas.modern_name: order-continuity / 'no jumps' conditions on principal ideals (cf. continuous posets, order topology)

ideas.what: Observation that posets coming from topological configurations usually fail this condition, so the strangeness relation is not detected by order alone
ideas.modern_name: failure of order-separation for spatial posets

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished axiomatic programme for analysis situs: abstract 'multi-objects' with strangeness and refinement relations, plus divisibility and separation axioms. The poset model shows that faithful and perfect models in dimension 1 are exactly the dense total orders (next page). The general axiom system and its classification of 1-dimensional models do not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: Lemme Pour que Mog L2 soit valable, il faut et il suffit que (i) L soit div. et que (ii) ∀x∈L, et a<b, on ait x || ]a,b[ ⇒ x≤a ou x≥b.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a combinatorial/synthetic approach to tame topology, an alternative to o-minimality. It might be compared with point-free topology (locales, mereotopology, region connection calculus), where 'disjoint interiors' versus 'strangeness' is a central issue.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's strangeness and refinement axioms closely resemble the contact/part-of axioms of mereotopology (Whitehead, de Laguna, region-based theories of space). His characterization of perfect 1-dim models as dense total orders parallels representation theorems for contact algebras. This link does not seem to have been made.
missed.quote: Ce n'est le plus souvent pas satisfait pour des ensembles ordonnés provenant de conditions topologiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could connect the unpublished Analysis situs to existing work in qualitative spatial reasoning and contact algebras.

deep.surprise_reason: The order theory itself is elementary (density, order-continuity). Interest lies only in its role within an unpublished axiomatic analysis situs programme, which is little known but whose individual lemmas are routine.
transcription_corrections: Previous page uses 'Mag 1-4' while this page uses 'Mog L1, L2'. The image reads 'Mog' here; these appear to be distinct axiom families (L for 'liens'?).
Add '(i)' / '(ii)' labels: the Lemma reads 'il faut et il suffit que (i) L soit div. et que (ii) ∀x∈L...', and (iii) is the 'Ou encore' form.
The interpolation above the crossed-out passage reads '(i) L soit div.', marking the later insertion of the divisibility hypothesis.
Final sentence possibly 'pour des ensembles ordonnés provenant de considérations/conditions topologiques'; the reading is uncertain.
